`veryMAD` estimates one median absolute deviation (MAD) threshold per selected
metric. Choose the metrics, tail directions, and transformations. Annotation
retains every input row; report mode returns flags and thresholds.

```{r}
#| label: setup
#| include: false
library(veryMAD)
```

## A basic QC workflow

This sequencing metadata example uses percentage points for `pct_mito`: 8
denotes 8%.

```{r}
sample_metadata <- data.frame(
  sample = paste0("sample_", 1:8),
  library_size = c(2.4e6, 2.5e6, 2.6e6, 2.7e6, 2.8e6, 2.6e6, 0.45e6, 2.5e6),
  detected_genes = c(12000, 12500, 13100, 12800, 13400, 12600, 1500, 12300),
  pct_mito = c(4, 5, 6, 5, 7, 6, 8, 29)
)

# Select the tail to review for each metric
qc_directions <- c(
  library_size = "lower",
  detected_genes = "lower",
  pct_mito = "upper"
)

# Add one flag per metric and a combined flag
qc_annotated <- mad_qc(
  sample_metadata,
  metrics = qc_directions,
  verbose = FALSE
)
```

The result keeps every row and adds logical flags:

```{r}
qc_annotated[, c("sample", "library_size_mad_outlier",
                 "detected_genes_mad_outlier", "pct_mito_mad_outlier",
                 "mad_qc_outlier")]
```

`mad_qc_outlier` is `TRUE` when any selected metric is flagged. Use the flags
to guide review in the analysis workflow.

## Inspect thresholds with a report

Use `output = "report"` to inspect thresholds and flags without adding columns
to the input.

```{r}
qc_report <- mad_qc(
  sample_metadata,
  metrics = qc_directions,
  output = "report",
  verbose = FALSE
)

qc_report$thresholds[, c("metric", "direction", "lower_raw",
                         "upper_raw", "status")]
qc_report$flags[, c("id", "mad_qc_outlier")]
```

The threshold table records each metric's status and observation counts.
